questions.q: What is the main strength of a centralized governance model?
options: It eliminates the need for any policy
It requires no coordination at all
Maximum consistency — one definition enforced everywhere
It scales infinitely regardless of organization size
questions.explain: Centralized governance keeps all decisions in one group, which maximizes consistency but can become a bottleneck at scale.

questions.q: In a decentralized model, what problem does the lesson say reliably recurs?
options: The exact conflicting-definitions problem governance exists to prevent, since there's no central coordination
Complete elimination of all data quality issues
Excessive central bureaucracy slowing every decision
A single enforced definition across all departments
questions.explain: Without central coordination, nothing forces consistency across departments — recreating the same conflicting-metric problem from Lesson 1.

questions.q: How does a federated model split responsibility, per the lesson?
options: Everything is governed locally, with no shared standards at all
Everything is governed centrally, with no local authority at all
A central body governs shared/cross-cutting data and standards; business units keep authority over their own local data
Governance authority rotates randomly between departments each quarter
questions.explain: Federated governance deliberately splits the difference: central standards for what needs consistency, local authority for everything else.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say federated governance has become the common default recommendation for larger, multi-business-unit organizations?
options: Because it requires no central coordination whatsoever
Because it is the cheapest and easiest model to implement
Because pure centralized doesn't scale and pure decentralized recreates the exact problem governance exists to solve
Because regulators legally mandate it for all companies
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that federated is recommended despite being the hardest to design — not because it's easy, but because the alternatives fail at scale.

questions.q: What practical test does the lesson suggest for identifying which model an organization is actually running?
options: Survey customers about their satisfaction
Check the company's stock price trend
Check whether a single body has authority to resolve cross-department data definition disagreements, or whether they just persist
Count how many people work in the IT department
questions.explain: The lesson's 'signals' test asks whether disputes actually get resolved by an authority, which reveals the real operating model regardless of what the org chart claims.
